(right panel) The Least Squares error can be thought of as the total area of the blue squares, having solid black error bars as sides. The cost function is called Least Squares because it allows us to determine a set of parameters whose corresponding line minimizes the sum of these square errors.

concepts.evidence: Least squares linear regression ... the cost as the sum of squared errors of a linear model of input against its corresponding output.
The Least Squares cost also takes in all inputs ... as well as the entire set of corresponding outputs
It is easy to get around most of this inefficiency by replacing explicit for loops with numerically equivalent operations performed using operations from the numpy library.
one can compute the gradient of the Least Squares cost in closed form as ∇g(w) = 2 Σ x_p (x_p^T w - y_p)
This single Newton step solution is often referred to as minimizing the Least Squares cost via its normal equations.
since the cost is a convex quadratic only a single Newton step can completely minimize it.
in performing Newton's method one can also compute the Hessian of the Least Squares cost by hand.
an alternative cost for linear regression called Least Absolute Deviations. This alternative cost function is much more robust to outliers in a dataset than the original Least Squares.
squaring the error increases the importance of larger errors ... the Least Squares cost produces linear models that tend to overfit to outliers in a dataset.
we can instead measure the absolute error for each desired approximation g_p(w) = |x_p^T w - y_p|
We then squared the difference between both sides of each desired approximation g_p(w) = (x_p^T w - y_p)^2
this cost function is also always convex regardless of the input dataset, since its second derivative is zero (almost everywhere) we can only use zero and first order methods to properly minimize it
given an input x0 ... we predict its output y0 by simply passing it along with our trained weights into our model as model(x0, w*) = y0
giving the so-called Mean Squared Error (or MSE for short) ... the average (or mean) squared error.

To reduce the affect of outliers and other large values, often the square root of this value is taken as a regression quality metric. This is referred to as the Root Mean Squared Error or RMSE for short.
Plugging in our learned model parameters along with the data into this cost computes the Mean Absolute Deviations (or MAD for short)
simple metrics for judging the quality of such a model
it is possible to weight these points in order to emphasize or de-emphasize their importance to a regression model. This practice is called weighted regression.

we recommend most users employ the automatic differentiator autograd to perform both gradient descent and Newton's method on our machine learning cost functions
